title: Lecture 2 — lines, circles, and conic sections
summary: Lines, circles, and conic sections all arise from coordinate equations. Slope and intercepts determine lines; distance and completing the square determine circles; focus and directrix or two foci determine parabolas and ellipses.
body: A line can be read from its slope, intercepts, or general equation. Distance equations describe circles and disks, and completing the square reveals a circle's centre and radius. Replacing $x$ by $x-h$ and $y$ by $y-k$ shifts a graph. Distance conditions then define the conics: equal distance from a focus and directrix gives a parabola, a constant sum of distances to two foci gives an ellipse, and a constant difference gives a hyperbola.
